title: Three Key Decorating Tips for Renters
paragraphs: When you don't own the house or apartment you live in, you usually can't do much to decorate it. This can make the space feel less like your own even though you're living there.
However, there are many easy ways to add some style to a rented home that won't cause problems with your landlord.
You might not be able to paint your walls, but that doesn't mean you can't use art to make them more interesting. Find pictures you really love and put them up in fun frames.

You do have to be a little careful with this though — a lot of landlords won't let you put nails in the wall. So, try using temporary adhesive strips that are strong enough to hold up your art, but can be taken down without damaging the wall.

Another easy way to decorate a rented house or apartment is to accessorize with soft furnishings like rugs, curtains, pillows and blankets. You can use all of these to bring more color into a room, and also make the space look more interesting with patterns and textures.

These can also cover things in your rented home that maybe you don't like. So if you don't like the floors, you can cover them in rugs! This even helps with your own furniture — a fun little blanket will make a boring sofa look much better.

Finally, try adding plants to your space. These add style and a feeling of calm to a room. Plants can also improve the air in your home, and if you grow plants you can eat — like basil and peppers — they can make your meals better too!
And of course, if you aren't sure you can keep a real plant alive, there's nothing wrong with getting some plastic ones instead!
